You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From d6d8cd2db236a9dd13dbc2d05843b3445cc964b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jenny Guanni Qu <qguanni@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 19:12:38 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nft_set_pipapo: fix stack out-of-bounds read in
 pipapo_drop()

pipapo_drop() passes rulemap[i + 1].n to pipapo_unmap() as the
to_offset argument on every iteration, including the last one where
i == m->field_count - 1. This reads one element past the end of the
stack-allocated rulemap array (declared as rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS]
with NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS == 16).

Although pipapo_unmap() returns early when is_last is true without
using the to_offset value, the argument is evaluated at the call site
before the function body executes, making this a genuine out-of-bounds
stack read confirmed by KASAN:

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in pipapo_drop+0x50c/0x57c [nf_tables]
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff8000810e71a4

  This frame has 1 object:
   [32, 160) 'rulemap'

  The buggy address is at offset 164 -- exactly 4 bytes past the end
  of the rulemap array.

Pass 0 instead of rulemap[i + 1].n on the last iteration to avoid
the out-of-bounds read.

Fixes: 3c4287f62044 ("nf_tables: Add set type for arbitrary concatenation of ranges")
Signed-off-by: Jenny Guanni Qu <qguanni@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c b/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
index a34632ae6048..7fd24e0cc428 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
@@ -1640,6 +1640,7 @@ static void pipapo_drop(struct nft_pipapo_match *m,
 	int i;
 
 	nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m) {
+		bool last = i == m->field_count - 1;
 		int g;
 
 		for (g = 0; g < f->groups; g++) {
@@ -1659,7 +1660,7 @@ static void pipapo_drop(struct nft_pipapo_match *m,
 		}
 
 		pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n,
-			     rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1);
+			     last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n, last);
 		if (pipapo_resize(f, f->rules, f->rules - rulemap[i].n)) {
 			/* We can ignore this, a failure to shrink tables down
 			 * doesn't make tables invalid.
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

### Modifications in `net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c`

- **Added a boolean variable `last`** inside the main loop of `pipapo_drop()` to indicate whether the current field index `i` is the last field (`i == m->field_count - 1`).

- **Changed the call to `pipapo_unmap()`**:  
  - The fourth argument (previously `rulemap[i + 1].n`) is now conditionally set: `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n`.  
  - The fifth argument (the `is_last` flag) is changed from `i == m->field_count - 1` to the already computed `last` value.

### Relationship between the changes

The core problem was an out-of-bounds stack read on the stack-allocated `rulemap` array. On the last loop iteration, `rulemap[i + 1]` accessed one element past the end of the array, even though `pipapo_unmap()` would later ignore that value because `is_last` was `true`. The fix decouples the computation of the out-of-bounds index from the call: it precomputes the `last` flag and passes a safe zero value when `last` is true, eliminating the read from `rulemap[i + 1]` on the final iteration while keeping the same logical behavior.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n,
             rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1);
```
Reason:
On the last iteration (i == m->field_count - 1), the expression `rulemap[i + 1].n` accesses an element past the end of the stack-allocated `rulemap` array (declared as `rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS]`). This causes a stack out-of-bounds read, even though the value is not used when the `is_last` argument is true, because the argument is evaluated at the call site.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
bool last = i == m->field_count - 1;
...
pipapo_unmap(...,
             last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n, last);
```
Reason:
By introducing a `last` flag and using a ternary expression `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n`, the out-of-bounds access is avoided on the final iteration: `0` is passed instead of the out-of-range `rulemap[i + 1].n`, preventing the undefined behavior.
